text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make code easier to read and understand, which helps developers find and fix problems faster. When you refactor, you clean up messy sections, remove duplicate logic, and give variables clearer names. This does not add new features or fix bugs; the program should behave exactly the same after refactoring. Regular refactoring also reduces technical debt, which builds up when teams take shortcuts to save time. By spending a little effort now, developers avoid much bigger problems later.
